items.title: CVE-2026-68820: Windows AFD.sys Zero-Day Actively Exploited by Lazarus Group in Operation Dream Job
items.summary: A use-after-free vulnerability in Windows Ancillary Function Driver (AFD.sys) allows local privilege escalation to SYSTEM. Patched in August 2026 Patch Tuesday alongside 397 other flaws, this zero-day was confirmed actively exploited in the wild before the patch was available. CVSS 7.0.
items.why: Check Point Research attributed active exploitation to North Korea's Lazarus APT within their ongoing Operation Dream Job campaign. Any existing foothold on a Windows machine becomes full SYSTEM-level control with no additional user interaction — a critical post-exploitation primitive widely in use before the patch dropped.
items.source: The Hacker News / Microsoft / Check Point Research

items.title: Trivy Vulnerability Scanner Infected with Infostealer in Supply Chain Attack — 153 GB of Cloud Credentials Stolen
items.summary: The popular open-source vulnerability scanner Trivy was compromised with infostealer malware, resulting in mass theft of Git logins, CI/CD secrets, cryptowallets, and cloud credentials from AWS, Samsung, and Cisco. All stolen data was aggregated into a 153 GB RAR archive.
items.why: Targeting trusted security and developer tooling is a devastating supply chain tactic. Organizations using Trivy for container or infrastructure scanning may have had cloud credentials and pipeline secrets silently exfiltrated — potentially granting attackers persistent access to production environments at scale.

items.title: Iran-Nexus APT 'Screening Serpens' Escalates Espionage Operations Across Five Countries with Novel RAT Families
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 is tracking Iranian state-linked threat group Screening Serpens, which dramatically escalated operations following a regional conflict beginning February 2026. The group has deployed two newly identified RAT variant families targeting organizations across up to five countries.
items.why: Nation-state actors tied to active geopolitical conflicts represent the highest-priority threat tier. Novel RAT family development indicates active capability investment, and the multi-country targeting scope shows espionage objectives extending well beyond the immediate conflict parties — any sector with geopolitical relevance should treat this as an active threat.

items.title: CVE-2026-59310: Critical VMware vCenter Auth Bypass Under Active APT Exploitation Spanning 47 Countries
items.summary: A critical authentication bypass in VMware vCenter allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code and achieve full vCenter environment takeover. Active APT exploitation has been confirmed, with a reverse SSH persistence framework deployed post-compromise. Attack infrastructure spans 361 unique IPs across 47 countries.
items.why: VMware vCenter manages virtual infrastructure at scale — a full unauthenticated compromise grants attackers control over entire datacenter environments. The breadth of attack infrastructure (47 countries, 361 IPs) and the deliberate persistence mechanism indicate a coordinated, well-resourced campaign rather than opportunistic exploitation.

items.title: Mandiant M-Trends 2026: New PROMPTFLUX & PROMPTSTEAL Malware Families Query LLMs at Runtime to Evade Detection
items.summary: Mandiant's M-Trends 2026 report — drawing on 500,000+ hours of frontline incident response — reveals a new class of AI-native malware. PROMPTFLUX and PROMPTSTEAL dynamically query large language models mid-execution to generate evasive commands and steal credentials. Mean attacker handoff time has collapsed to just 22 seconds.
items.why: This is a genuinely novel attack class: malware that adapts at runtime using AI, fundamentally undermining signature-based and behavioral detection. The 22-second handoff metric signals that defenders now have an extraordinarily narrow window to detect and contain initial intrusions before lateral movement begins — traditional incident response timelines are no longer valid.
